key_insight: Raising the O2/C2H2 ratio during flame spraying densified Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings, reducing porosity and roughness while improving adhesion, with peak microhardness at an intermediate ratio.
engineering_relevance: Tuning flame-spray gas ratio offers a practical process lever to optimize wear- and corrosion-resistant coating quality on stainless-steel substrates.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings onto AISI 321 steel.
Varied O2/C2H2 ratio to 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Monitored spray conditions with Accuraspray 4.0 and measured porosity, roughness, microhardness, and adhesion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports porosity decreasing from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, roughness from 4.70 ± 0.09 µm to 2.99 ± 0.11 µm, adhesion increasing from 22.14 ± 4.3 MPa to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa, and a maximum microhardness of 1051.7 HV at O2/C2H2 = 1.1.
watch_item: Results are limited to the tested gas-ratio window and coating system, so the same optimum may not transfer directly to other substrates, torch setups, or service conditions.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
